questions.stem: Leadership is best defined as:

options.A: The formal authority granted by an organization to a manager
options.B: The process of influencing people to strive willingly and enthusiastically toward the achievement of group goals
options.C: The act of issuing directives to subordinates
options.D: A system of rules and regulations governing employee behaviour

questions.explanation: Leadership centers on influence and voluntary enthusiasm rather than just formal command.

questions.stem: Which of the following distinguishes a leader from a manager?

options.A: A leader administers while a manager innovates
options.B: A leader accepts the status quo while a manager challenges it
options.C: A leader focuses on people while a manager focuses on systems and structure
options.D: A leader relies on controls while a manager inspires trust

questions.explanation: Managers deal with the mechanics of the organization, whereas leaders deal with the people within it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a leader, NOT a manager?

options.B: Maintains

questions.explanation: Leaders are change agents who innovate and develop new ideas, while managers maintain existing ones.

questions.stem: A manager is said to 'do things right' while a leader is said to:

options.B: Follow all procedures

questions.explanation: Doing things right is efficiency (management); doing the right things is effectiveness (leadership).

questions.stem: Which view of leadership emphasizes that it involves influence, group processes, personality, and goal achievement?

options.B: Traditional management view

questions.explanation: This approach recognizes that leadership is complex and involves many different factors simultaneously.

questions.stem: What does a visionary leader accomplish by using discretion and authority?

options.B: Achieves objectives and gains willing obedience of subordinates

questions.explanation: Visionary leadership uses influence to get people to follow a path because they want to, not because they have to.

questions.stem: Why are not all managers considered effective leaders?

options.B: Effective leadership requires traits and behaviours that go beyond managerial functions
options.C: Managers only work in organized sectors
options.D: Leadership and management are identical roles

questions.explanation: A manager can be good at planning and budgeting but fail to inspire or influence people.

questions.stem: According to Warren and Benin, a manager has a 'short-range view' while a leader has a:

options.B: Long-range view

questions.explanation: Leaders look at the future horizon (strategy) while managers focus on immediate results (tactics).

questions.stem: A leader 'challenges' the status quo while a manager:

options.B: Develops

questions.explanation: Management is about stability and order, while leadership is about change and improvement.

questions.stem: The ability of a good leader to turn a hopeless situation into a winning one demonstrates:

options.B: Technical expertise

questions.explanation: Great leaders navigate crises by finding strategic opportunities where others see failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an essential ingredient of effective leadership?

options.B: The ability to use power effectively

questions.explanation: Power is the tool leaders use to influence others; using it responsibly is key to success.

questions.stem: The ability of a leader to understand subordinates' needs, expectations and the situation is called:

options.B: Ability to inspire

questions.explanation: Comprehension in leadership means deeply understanding the diverse motivations of your team.

questions.stem: Which ingredient of leadership refers to motivating subordinates to work with zeal even in difficult situations?

options.B: Ability to comprehend

questions.explanation: Inspiration is what keeps a group moving forward with passion when things get tough.

questions.stem: Leadership style as an ingredient requires the leader to:

options.A: Impose strict rules without considering employee needs
options.B: Design an environment for efficient performance and identify motivational needs
options.D: Delegate all responsibilities to middle management

questions.explanation: A leader's style shapes the work environment and dictates how well employees are motivated.

questions.stem: Legitimate power is obtained by a leader through:

options.B: Technical expertise
options.C: Virtue of formal appointment in a position

questions.explanation: Legitimate power comes from the formal hierarchy or 'title' given by the organization.

questions.stem: Expert power is derived from a leader's:

options.B: Control over rewards and punishments

questions.explanation: Followers listen because the leader possesses specific skills or information they need.

questions.stem: Referent power arises from:

options.A: Formal authority granted by the organization
options.B: Followers' admiration and identification with the leader
options.C: The leader's control over financial resources

questions.explanation: Referent power is based on personal charisma; people follow because they like and respect the leader.

questions.stem: Reward power refers to the leader's ability to:

options.B: Provide positive outcomes for desired behaviour

questions.explanation: This is the power to influence others by offering things they value (raises, praise, etc.).

questions.stem: Coercive power involves a leader's use of:

options.B: Technical skills
options.C: Punishment or threat of punishment to influence behaviour

questions.explanation: Coercive power relies on fear and the ability to penalize followers.

questions.stem: Inspiration in leadership often comes from a leader's charismatic personality because:

options.B: Followers are drawn to and motivated by leaders they admire
options.C: It replaces the need for technical skills

questions.explanation: People are more likely to be inspired by a leader they feel a personal connection to.

questions.stem: The three types of skills required at different levels of management are:

options.B: Technical, human, and conceptual skills

questions.explanation: These are the three pillars of management competence identified by Robert Katz.

questions.stem: Human skills in leadership are important for:

options.B: Middle management only

questions.explanation: Since all managers work with people, human skills are universally required at every level.

questions.stem: Technical skills involve the ability to:

options.A: View the organization in strategic terms
options.B: Understand interpersonal relationships
options.C: Know and apply technical aspects of operations and machinery

questions.explanation: Technical skills are the 'know-how' related to specific processes or tools.

questions.stem: Conceptual skills are MOST critical at which level of management?

options.B: Operational level

questions.explanation: Top leaders need to see the 'big picture' and understand how the whole organization fits together.

questions.stem: As managers move higher in an organization, which skill becomes increasingly important?

options.B: Physical skill

questions.explanation: Senior roles require more abstract thinking and strategy than hands-on technical work.

questions.stem: Human skills are concerned with:

options.B: Operation of machinery and tools
options.C: Interpersonal relationships and obtaining willing cooperation from others

questions.explanation: Human skills allow a manager to lead, communicate, and resolve conflict effectively.

questions.stem: Conceptual skills involve the ability to:

options.B: Manage interpersonal conflicts
options.C: View the organization in strategic terms and understand long-term implications

questions.explanation: It is the ability to understand complex situations and see the organization as a unified whole.

questions.stem: Lower-level managers spend more time on which type of skill?

options.B: Strategic skill

questions.explanation: Supervisors deal directly with the work being done, requiring high technical proficiency.

questions.stem: Which leadership style involves concentrating power and authority within the leader and expecting high compliance from subordinates?

options.B: Laissez-faire leadership

questions.explanation: In this style, the leader makes all decisions and expects followers to obey without question.

questions.stem: Communication in autocratic leadership primarily flows:

options.B: Horizontally among peers

questions.explanation: It is one-way communication: the leader gives orders, and the followers receive them.

questions.stem: A benevolent autocrat is best described as a leader who:

options.A: Equally shares decision-making with all subordinates
options.B: Listens to followers before making their own decisions

questions.explanation: A benevolent autocrat cares about the followers' input but still retains ultimate decision-making power.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary disadvantage of autocratic leadership?

options.B: Low morale among subordinates whose views are not considered

questions.explanation: Employees often feel undervalued and demotivated when they have no voice in the workplace.

questions.stem: Democratic or participative leadership is characterized by:

options.B: Subordinates having complete freedom without leader involvement
options.C: Leader consulting subordinates and encouraging participation in decision-making
options.D: Strict hierarchical control and one-way communication

questions.explanation: This style involves collaboration and sharing the decision-making process.

questions.stem: Which leadership style typically results in higher quality decisions due to greater subordinate input?

options.B: Exploitive-authoritative

questions.explanation: Tapping into the collective intelligence of the group often leads to more informed outcomes.

questions.stem: A major disadvantage of democratic leadership is:

options.B: Lack of employee participation

questions.explanation: Consulting with others and reaching a consensus takes more time than issuing a single order.

questions.stem: Laissez-faire leadership is also called:

options.B: Free rein leadership

questions.explanation: It comes from the French term 'allow to do,' where the leader steps back and lets the group lead themselves.

questions.stem: In laissez-faire leadership, the leader's primary role is to:

options.B: Closely supervise all employee activities
options.C: Provide information when requested and act as a contact between departments

questions.explanation: The leader acts more like a resource or consultant than a traditional 'boss'.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is MOST likely to result in lack of group cohesiveness and potential chaos?

options.B: Autocratic leadership

questions.explanation: Without direction, a group can become uncoordinated or work in conflicting directions.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is most appropriate in emergency situations requiring quick decisions?

options.B: Democratic

questions.explanation: When speed is vital, a single person taking charge is more effective than group discussion.

questions.stem: Free-rein or laissez-faire leadership is most effective in which type of work setting?

options.A: Mass production factories requiring strict compliance
options.B: Emergency response situations
options.C: Research and Development where professionals work autonomously
options.D: Customer service environments requiring rapid responses

questions.explanation: Highly skilled experts often perform better when they are given the freedom to innovate.

questions.stem: In democratic leadership, policy is determined by:

options.B: The group assisted by the leader

questions.explanation: The leader facilitates the discussion, but the group ultimately shapes the policy.

questions.stem: In autocratic leadership, future courses of action are:

options.A: Discussed and agreed upon by the group
options.B: Left to individual discretion
options.C: Dictated by the manager one at a time without revealing future plans
options.D: Determined through formal strategic planning sessions

questions.explanation: Keeping subordinates in the dark about the 'big picture' maintains the leader's power and control.

questions.stem: Mc Murry argued for 'benevolent autocracy' because:

options.B: Most top managers have hard-driving, autocratic personalities and significant decisions must be made by top management
options.C: Democratic management always leads to better results
options.D: Subordinates are fully capable of self-direction

questions.explanation: It acknowledges that some organizations and leaders operate best with a firm but caring hand.

questions.stem: Participation may sometimes be interpreted by employees as:

options.B: Their right to veto managerial decisions
options.C: A reduction in their job security

questions.explanation: If not managed well, employees may wrongly assume that participation means they have the final say.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the autocratic leader's approach to praise and criticism?

options.B: Absent no praise or criticism given
options.C: Personal in nature, keeping subordinates at a distance
options.D: Equally distributed among all team members

questions.explanation: Feedback in an autocratic setting is often subjective and used to maintain the leader's status.

questions.stem: Prof Rensis Likert conducted his leadership studies at which university?

options.B: Yale University

questions.explanation: Likert's famous research on management systems originated at the University of Michigan.

questions.stem: Likert's model of management consists of how many systems?

options.B: Three

questions.explanation: Likert identified four distinct management styles ranging from exploitive to participative.

questions.stem: Which of Likert's systems is characterized by highly autocratic management, no trust in subordinates, and motivation through fear and punishment?

options.B: System-3: Consultative

questions.explanation: This is the most rigid and authoritarian of Likert's four systems.

questions.stem: In Likert's System-2 (Benevolent-authoritative), decision-making authority is:

options.B: Limited and delegated to a minimum extent

questions.explanation: While slightly more open than System 1, control remains very much at the top.

questions.stem: System-3 in Likert's model is called:

options.B: Benevolent-authoritative

questions.explanation: Managers in this system seek input from subordinates but make the final decisions themselves.

questions.stem: Which of Likert's systems involves substantial but not full trust in subordinates?

options.B: System-2

questions.explanation: There is a significant amount of trust, but it hasn't reached the complete partnership level of System 4.

questions.stem: Moving from System-1 to System-4 in Likert's model represents a shift from:

options.B: Technical to human skill focus
options.C: Autocratic and exploitive to participative and group-centred management

questions.explanation: The scale moves from controlling individuals to empowering the whole group.

questions.stem: In System-1 of Likert's model, communication flows:

options.B: Primarily downward only

questions.explanation: This system relies on orders being pushed from the top down.

questions.stem: Which of Likert's systems involves the highest degree of group participation, mutual trust, and shared decision-making?

options.B: System-2

questions.explanation: System 4 (Participative) is considered the ideal system for employee engagement and productivity.

questions.stem: Likert's model is primarily used to understand:

options.B: Patterns and styles of managerial leadership and their effect on human behaviour

questions.explanation: It focuses on the 'human' side of management and how style affects the workplace climate.

questions.stem: The Trait Theory of Leadership is also called:

options.B: Situational theory
options.C: Great man's theory or attribute theory

questions.explanation: This older theory suggests that leaders are born with specific traits that others lack.

questions.stem: Davis identified that effective leaders tend to have a higher degree of _______ than their followers.

options.B: Financial wealth

questions.explanation: Research suggests leaders often possess slightly higher cognitive abilities than those they lead.

questions.stem: 'Social maturity and breadth' as a leadership trait refers to:

options.B: Emotional maturity and a broad range of interests

questions.explanation: Leaders need emotional stability and the ability to see things from many perspectives.

questions.stem: Leaders with 'inner motivation and achievement drives':

options.A: Depend heavily on external rewards for motivation
options.B: Seek out new goals once they achieve the previous one
options.D: Rely on subordinates to set their goals

questions.explanation: Great leaders are self-driven and constantly push for higher levels of success.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a task-related characteristic identified by Stogdill in effective leaders?

options.B: Achievement drive, persistence, and initiative

questions.explanation: These traits are focused on getting the actual work done and overcoming obstacles.

questions.stem: Cooperativeness, interpersonal skills, and administrative ability are categorized by Stogdill as:

options.B: Personality traits

questions.explanation: These traits allow a leader to work effectively within the social structure of the group.

questions.stem: A major limitation of the Trait Theory of Leadership is that:

options.A: It provides too much guidance on leadership development
options.B: It gives no guidance on how much of any trait a leader should have
options.C: It focuses only on physical traits
options.D: It applies universally to all cultures

questions.explanation: The theory identifies traits but fails to explain the 'mix' or degree needed for success.

questions.stem: Most of the traits identified in successful leaders by Stogdill are actually:

options.B: Financially determined
options.C: Patterns of behaviour rather than fixed traits

questions.explanation: This suggests that leadership is about how you act, which can be learned, rather than just how you are born.

questions.stem: Davis found leadership characteristics to be more prevalent in:

options.B: Lower-level supervisors

questions.explanation: Those who rise to higher management usually exhibit more distinct leadership traits.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a personality trait identified by Stogdill?

options.B: Persistence

questions.explanation: Personality traits describe the internal temperament of the leader.

questions.stem: The 'human relations attitude' as a leadership trait means the leader:

options.B: Understands that to accomplish tasks, they must be considerate of others
options.D: Maintains strict professional distance from subordinates

questions.explanation: This attitude recognizes that tasks are completed through people, requiring empathy and respect.

questions.stem: Why is Trait Theory considered inconclusive?

options.B: Not all leaders possess all traits, and there is no guidance on the degree of each trait needed
options.C: It only applies to military leaders
options.D: It focuses exclusively on lower-level management

questions.explanation: There are many 'great' leaders who don't fit the standard trait profile, making the theory unreliable.

questions.stem: Contingency or situational leadership recognizes that:

options.B: The best leadership style depends on the specific situation
options.C: Democratic leadership always produces the best results
options.D: Leadership traits are fixed and cannot change

questions.explanation: This modern approach says that the 'best' way to lead changes based on the context.

questions.stem: Path-goal theory of leadership focuses on:

options.A: Identifying personality traits of effective leaders
options.B: How leaders can assist followers in defining and achieving their goals
options.C: Classifying leaders into autocratic and democratic types
options.D: The relationship between management systems and financial performance

questions.explanation: A leader's job is to clarify the path and remove obstacles for their team.

questions.stem: Transformational leadership primarily involves:

options.A: Maintaining current organizational systems without change
options.B: Inspiring, motivating, and transforming followers to achieve beyond expected performance
options.C: Focusing only on short-term operational goals

questions.explanation: Transformational leaders change both the organization and the people within it.

questions.stem: Charismatic leadership is associated with:

options.B: Financial incentive systems
options.C: A leader's exceptional personal qualities that inspire devotion and commitment in followers

questions.explanation: Charisma is a personal 'magnetism' that draws people toward a leader.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the Managerial Grid approach to leadership?

options.A: It classifies leaders based on physical traits
options.B: It plots leadership styles based on concern for people and concern for production
options.C: It focuses only on motivational needs of employees
options.D: It establishes a hierarchy of leadership systems

questions.explanation: The grid (developed by Blake and Mouton) balances the need for results with the need for people.

questions.stem: Good leadership requires that an organization's practices include which of the following?

options.A: Closed communication systems and centralized decision-making
options.B: Appropriate reward systems, freedom of action, recognition, and open communication
options.C: Strict supervision and limited employee autonomy

questions.explanation: These factors create a healthy organizational climate where leadership can thrive.

questions.stem: A leader who works in identical conditions as subordinates and does not show signs of tiredness is demonstrating:

options.B: Laissez-faire detachment
options.C: Appropriate leadership style and genuine involvement with the team

questions.explanation: Leading by example is one of the most powerful ways to influence others.

questions.stem: Willing obedience from subordinates is achieved when a leader:

options.B: Fulfills the desires, wants, and needs of followers

questions.explanation: When people feel their needs are being met, they are more likely to follow willingly.

questions.stem: A leader should identify each individual's capabilities and inspire them. This relates to which ingredient?

options.B: Leadership style

questions.explanation: Inspiration is about seeing the potential in others and helping them reach it.

questions.stem: In terms of organizational goal achievement, leadership is MOST effective when followers work:

options.B: Willingly and with zeal toward group goals

questions.explanation: Enthusiastic participation leads to better results than forced compliance.

questions.stem: An appropriate leadership style must be selected based on:

options.B: External market conditions only
options.C: Organizational climate, environment, and the needs of subordinates

questions.explanation: A leader must adapt their style to fit the specific world they are leading in.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a leader's reconciliatory approach?

options.B: Seeking to bring conflicting parties together and find mutually acceptable solutions
options.D: Delegating all conflict resolution to HR

questions.explanation: Reconciliation is about fixing relationships and finding a path forward for the team.

questions.stem: Line authority allows a leader to:

options.B: Conduct strategic planning
options.C: Influence and direct subordinates through the organizational hierarchy

questions.explanation: Line authority is the formal 'vertical' power to give instructions to subordinates.

questions.stem: Which type of organizational structure does System-1 (Exploitive-authoritative) management characterize?

options.B: Matrix organization

questions.explanation: Rigid, top-down structures are where exploitive-authoritative styles are usually found.

questions.stem: The contribution of Warren and Benin to leadership theory was primarily in:

options.B: Distinguishing between managerial and leadership characteristics

questions.explanation: They helped define why leading people is fundamentally different from managing tasks.

questions.stem: For leadership to be effective in an organization, what must the leader identify?

options.B: External competitors
options.C: Motivational needs, desires, and aspirations of subordinates

questions.explanation: You cannot lead effectively if you don't know what drives your people.

questions.stem: When a leader evolves techniques to lead toward a win-win strategy under difficult conditions, they are demonstrating:

options.B: Technical expertise

questions.explanation: Being able to change tactics to find a solution that benefits everyone is a mark of a great leader.

questions.stem: The concept of 'benevolent autocracy' argues that:

options.A: Employees should always participate in all decisions
options.B: A compassionate but firm leadership approach is best in certain organizational contexts
options.C: All authority should be distributed equally
options.D: Technical skills are the primary driver of leadership success

questions.explanation: Sometimes a group needs clear direction, but it must be delivered with care for the people.

questions.stem: A leader who is loyal to subordinates and follows an appropriate leadership style is exercising:

options.B: Technical management

questions.explanation: Loyalty to followers builds the trust necessary for effective leadership.

questions.stem: The difference between autocratic and democratic leadership in task assignment is that in democratic leadership:

options.A: The manager dictates tasks one at a time
options.B: Members can work with whomever they choose
options.D: Tasks are determined purely by technical requirements

questions.explanation: Democratic styles allow for more autonomy in how work is structured and with whom people collaborate.

questions.stem: In laissez-faire leadership, who bears the primary responsibility for determining techniques and processes?

options.B: The organizational hierarchy
options.C: Individual members or the group itself

questions.explanation: The leader steps out of the way and lets the experts decide how to get the job done.

questions.stem: Leadership that promotes individual growth and freedom of action for goal setting is associated with:

options.B: System-1 management

questions.explanation: By providing complete freedom, this style forces individuals to grow and set their own direction.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly contrasts autocratic and laissez-faire leadership?

options.A: Both give equal freedom to subordinates
options.B: Autocratic centralizes decision-making while laissez-faire gives full freedom to subordinates
options.C: Both encourage equal participation in decision-making
options.D: Laissez-faire is more authoritarian than autocratic

questions.explanation: They are at opposite ends of the spectrum regarding leader control versus follower freedom.

questions.stem: A participative leader differs from a laissez-faire leader in that the participative leader:

options.B: Actively consults and remains involved in decision-making with subordinates

questions.explanation: A participative leader is part of the team, whereas a laissez-faire leader is largely absent.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly reflects Mc Murry's view on security-seeking employees?

options.A: All employees desire to participate in decision-making
options.B: Many employees in large bureaucracies are security seekers who do not wish to share in decision-making
options.C: Security seekers are always the most productive employees
options.D: Security needs are irrelevant to leadership effectiveness

questions.explanation: Some people prefer the safety of being told what to do rather than the pressure of making decisions.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is most associated with innovation and creativity in subordinates?

options.B: Autocratic

questions.explanation: When people have a voice, they are more likely to share new and creative ideas.

questions.stem: Davis's four leadership characteristics apply most strongly to:

options.B: Middle and upper-level managers

questions.explanation: These roles are where complex leadership traits are most vital for organizational success.

questions.stem: The physical traits identified by Stogdill include:

options.B: Cooperativeness and interpersonal skills

questions.explanation: Stogdill's early research looked at how physical characteristics might correlate with leadership roles.

questions.stem: Which of the following leadership theories emphasizes that there is no single best way to lead?

options.B: Great man's theory

questions.explanation: This theory states that effectiveness is all about the 'fit' between style and situation.

questions.stem: In the context of democratic leadership, the quality of decisions is described as:

options.B: Equal to autocratic leadership
options.C: Better compared to autocratic leadership due to subordinate involvement

questions.explanation: More perspectives and 'buy-in' from the group generally lead to better executed and sounder choices.

questions.stem: In Likert's System-2, the manager's approach to upward communication is:

options.B: Completely suppressed
options.C: Minimum but with some input from subordinates allowed

questions.explanation: In System 2, information mainly flows down, with only tiny amounts allowed back up.

questions.stem: Leadership instills which of the following values in an organization?

options.A: Passive compliance and avoidance of risk
options.B: Honesty, calculated risk-taking, and genuine concern for employees and customers
options.C: Strict adherence to financial targets only

questions.explanation: Great leaders build a culture that values people and ethical growth.

questions.stem: The goal of effective leadership in any organization is to:

options.B: Ensure strict compliance with rules
options.C: Achieve organizational goals through inspired, willing effort of followers

questions.explanation: The ultimate test of leadership is whether the group successfully reaches its goals with passion and commitment.

questions.stem: When a leader maintains an open communication system and informal, cordial behaviour, they are:

options.B: Creating a conducive organizational climate for motivation and performance

questions.explanation: Openness and cordiality build trust, which is a foundational element for a high-performance work environment.

questions.stem: Stogdill's research on leadership traits showed that adaptability and aggressiveness are categorized as:

options.B: Physical traits

questions.explanation: Stogdill identified internal behavioral dispositions like adaptability as part of the leader's personality profile.

questions.stem: The concept that leadership involves 'bringing people to a high pitch of devotion to duty' suggests:

options.B: Financial incentivization

questions.explanation: Devotion to duty implies that followers are internally moved to perform at their best, rather than being forced.

questions.stem: Which of the following reflects the contingency approach to leadership?

options.A: There is one universally best leadership style
options.B: The same style should be used regardless of context
options.C: Managers should adapt their leadership style to fit different situations

questions.explanation: The contingency approach states that leadership effectiveness is 'contingent' upon matching the right style to the right situation.

questions.stem: In which type of organization are democratic leadership practices most widely used?

options.B: Military emergency operations

questions.explanation: In knowledge-work, the leader relies on the expertise of subordinates, making a participative/democratic style essential.

questions.stem: A leader who uses power very little and gives subordinates full independence is practicing:

options.B: Democratic leadership

questions.explanation: Laissez-faire (Free-rein) is characterized by a hands-off approach where the group makes most decisions.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes Likert's System-1 approach to decision-making?

options.B: Decision-making is shared between management and subordinates
options.C: Decision-making is concentrated at the top level only
options.D: Decisions are made by external consultants

questions.explanation: System-1 is exploitive-authoritative, meaning all power and decisions flow strictly from the top down.

questions.stem: Leadership is often described as 'human in nature' because it:

options.B: Relies on interpersonal relationships and influence rather than just systems

questions.explanation: Unlike technical management, leadership is fundamentally about the psychological and social interaction between people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a core ingredient of leadership?

options.B: Ability to inspire

questions.explanation: Accounting is a specific technical skill, whereas power, inspiration, and empathy are universal leadership 'ingredients'.

questions.stem: A leader's 'ability to comprehend' refers to:

options.B: Understanding that people have different motivating forces at different times

questions.explanation: A leader must realize that what motivates one person today might not motivate another tomorrow.

questions.stem: The 'ability to inspire' in leadership involves:

options.B: Motivating followers to apply their full capabilities to a project

questions.explanation: Inspiration makes followers want to give their maximum effort toward a shared vision.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is most likely to result in the highest employee satisfaction in a research lab?

options.B: Exploitive

questions.explanation: Experts in R&D value autonomy and the freedom to explore ideas without constant interference.

questions.stem: An autocratic leader typically makes decisions:

options.B: Through group voting
options.D: Only after a consensus is reached

questions.explanation: Autocracy is defined by centralized authority where the leader's word is final.

questions.stem: The 'benevolent-authoritative' system (System 2) is characterized by:

options.B: A condescending confidence and trust in subordinates

questions.explanation: System-2 is 'paternalistic'—the leader is kind but still maintains absolute control.

questions.stem: In Likert’s System 3 (Consultative), the flow of communication is:

options.B: Upward only
options.C: Both vertical and horizontal, but major decisions are made at the top

questions.explanation: Communication is more open, but the leader still holds the 'veto' and final decision power.

questions.stem: Which of Likert’s systems is considered the most effective for long-term organizational success?

options.B: System-2: Benevolent-authoritative

questions.explanation: System-4 fosters the highest levels of trust and commitment, leading to sustainable long-term performance.

questions.stem: Trait theory suggests that leaders are:

options.B: Trained in 2 weeks

questions.explanation: The 'Great Man' theory posits that leadership is a set of inherent biological/personality traits.

questions.stem: A criticism of the Great Man theory is that:

options.B: It ignores the influence of the situation on leadership effectiveness
options.C: It focuses too much on teamwork

questions.explanation: Someone with 'leader traits' might succeed in one context but fail in another; the theory ignores this.

questions.stem: Fiedler’s contingency model proposes that leadership effectiveness depends on:

options.B: The match between leadership style and the degree of situational control

questions.explanation: Fiedler believed that leaders have a fixed style and must be placed in situations that favor that style.

questions.stem: In the Managerial Grid, a (1,9) style represents:

options.B: Low concern for people, low concern for production
options.C: High concern for people, low concern for production

questions.explanation: Often called 'Country Club' management, it focuses on keeping people happy at the expense of output.

questions.stem: A (9,1) leadership style on the Managerial Grid is:

options.B: Country Club management

questions.explanation: This style prioritizes production and treats people as mere tools or 'cogs' in the machine.

questions.stem: The (9,9) style on the Managerial Grid is known as:

options.B: Dictatorial

questions.explanation: (9,9) is the ideal on the grid, representing high commitment to both the people and the mission.

questions.stem: Path-Goal theory suggests that a leader’s job is to:

options.B: Clear the path for subordinates to reach their goals

questions.explanation: The leader acts as a guide, providing the support and resources needed to make the 'path' to the goal easy.

questions.stem: Transformational leaders focus on:

options.B: Changing the organization’s culture and the followers' values

questions.explanation: Transformation implies deep change in how people think and what they believe about their work.

questions.stem: Transactional leadership is based on:

options.B: Exchanges between the leader and followers (rewards for performance)

questions.explanation: It is a 'contractual' relationship: 'If you do this work, I will give you this reward'.

questions.stem: Charismatic leaders influence others through:

options.B: Their personal charm and magnetic personality

questions.explanation: Followers are drawn to the leader's personality and are willing to follow them because of it.

questions.stem: Servant leadership emphasizes:

options.B: Putting the needs of followers first

questions.explanation: The servant leader believes that by helping employees grow, the organization naturally succeeds.

questions.stem: Situational leadership theory was developed by:

options.B: Hersey and Blanchard

questions.explanation: They argued that leaders must adjust their style based on the 'maturity' or readiness of the followers.

questions.stem: According to situational leadership, if a follower is 'unable and unwilling,' the leader should use a:

options.B: Selling style

questions.explanation: When readiness is low, the leader must provide specific directions and closely supervise performance.

questions.stem: If a follower is 'able and willing,' the leader should use a:

options.B: Selling style

questions.explanation: High-readiness followers require very little supervision or direction.

questions.stem: Power is defined as:

options.B: The ability to influence the behavior of others
options.D: The budget allocated to a manager

questions.explanation: Power is the actual capacity to get things done, regardless of whether it is formal or informal.

questions.stem: Legitimate power is also known as:

options.B: Personal power

questions.explanation: It is the power that comes specifically from the 'position' or office a person holds.

questions.stem: Expert power comes from:

options.B: Specialized knowledge or skills

questions.explanation: People follow an expert because they believe that person knows more than they do about the task.

questions.stem: Referent power is based on:

options.B: Followers' identification with or liking of the leader

questions.explanation: It is based on the follower's desire to be like the leader or be associated with them.

questions.stem: Coercive power relies on:

options.B: Fear and the threat of punishment

questions.explanation: Coercion is about forcing compliance through negative consequences.

questions.stem: Reward power is the ability to:

options.B: Withhold information

questions.explanation: This power stems from the leader's control over things that the subordinates value.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a 'Manager' but NOT a 'Leader'?

options.B: Administers and maintains

questions.explanation: Managers focus on upkeep and order; leaders focus on change and innovation.

questions.stem: A 'Leader' is someone who:

options.B: Accepts the status quo

questions.explanation: Leaders are creators of new paths and ideas rather than just maintainers of old ones.

questions.stem: Which of the following demonstrates the ‘ability to use power effectively’ in leadership?

options.A: Using only one type of power
options.B: Strategically combining expert, referent, reward, and coercive power

questions.explanation: An effective leader knows which type of power to 'pull' depending on the situation and person.

questions.stem: In democratic leadership, role formation and task assignment are:

options.B: Dictated by the leader

questions.explanation: Involvement in the process ensures better 'buy-in' and use of individual strengths.

questions.stem: A leader who does not reveal future plans and dictates tasks one at a time is practicing:

options.B: Democratic leadership

questions.explanation: Withholding information is a common tactic to maintain total control and dependency.

questions.stem: Which of the following is associated with ‘long-range view’ in leadership?

options.B: Strategic planning and visionary thinking

questions.explanation: Leaders look years ahead to ensure the organization is moving in the right direction.

questions.stem: The text identifies that a successful leader has the ability to:

options.B: Turn a hopeless situation into a winning one

questions.explanation: Resilience and the ability to pivot during a crisis are hallmarks of great leadership.

questions.stem: Leadership effectiveness is measured by:

options.A: How much the leader is paid
options.B: Goal achievement and follower satisfaction

questions.explanation: Success is found when the mission is accomplished AND the people feel motivated.

questions.stem: A leader who 'does the right thing' is focusing on:

options.B: Efficiency

questions.explanation: Effectiveness means choosing the correct goal or path to take.

questions.stem: A manager who 'does things right' is focusing on:

options.B: Efficiency

questions.explanation: Efficiency is about performing a task correctly and with minimal waste.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is best for a team of highly skilled experts?

options.B: Exploitive

questions.explanation: Experts perform best when they are trusted with the autonomy to use their skills.

questions.stem: Which leadership style is best for a crisis?

options.B: Democratic

questions.explanation: In a crisis, fast decisions and clear commands are more important than consensus.

questions.stem: Democratic leadership is also known as:

options.B: Participative leadership

questions.explanation: Participation is the core mechanic of the democratic style.

questions.stem: In System 1 (Likert), motivation is achieved through:

options.B: Fear, threats, and punishment

questions.explanation: This is a 'negative' motivation style used in exploitive environments.

questions.stem: In System 4 (Likert), motivation is achieved through:

options.B: Micromanagement

questions.explanation: Followers are motivated by being part of the process and receiving fair compensation.

questions.stem: Leadership theories are studied in organizational behaviour primarily because:

options.B: Leadership is one of the most important aspects of human behaviour

questions.explanation: Human behavior is what drives organizations; leadership is the 'engine' of that behavior.

questions.stem: A leader who ‘asks what and why’ is demonstrating:

options.B: Critical and questioning leadership thinking

questions.explanation: Great leaders don't just follow orders; they seek to understand the purpose behind every action.

questions.stem: The effectiveness of leadership is ultimately measured by:

options.B: The extent to which followers achieve organizational goals willingly

questions.explanation: Willing effort is the 'magic ingredient' that distinguishes leadership from simple coercion.

questions.stem: Which of the following reflects good organizational practices?

options.B: Recognition, reward systems, and open communication

questions.explanation: These practices create a positive culture where leadership can flourish.

questions.stem: A leader in a democratic setting ensures that:

options.B: Subordinates participate in decision-making
options.C: Only the leader's ideas are used

questions.explanation: Shared decision-making is the hallmark of the democratic setting.

questions.stem: The concept of leadership focusing on ‘people’ implies:

options.B: Human motivation is central to organizational success

questions.explanation: If people are motivated and aligned, the business results will follow.

questions.stem: The MOST appropriate behaviour when a leader has found the best solution is:

options.B: Consulting subordinates to gain their buy-in
options.D: Waiting for someone else to suggest it

questions.explanation: Even if the solution is perfect, people won't execute it well if they don't feel involved.

questions.stem: Subordinates ‘promote what the leader desires’ when the leader has:

options.B: Inspirational leadership that earns commitment

questions.explanation: Inspiration aligns the follower's desires with the leader's vision.

questions.stem: A leader who uses the same style regardless of the situation is likely to:

options.B: Experience suboptimal performance

questions.explanation: A 'one-size-fits-all' approach fails when the environment or team readiness changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of having a leader rather than just a manager?

options.B: Greater ability to inspire and innovate

questions.explanation: Leaders bring the 'spirit' and 'vision' that routine management lacks.

questions.stem: Likert's model is valuable because it:

options.B: Classifies leadership styles from authoritarian to participative

questions.explanation: It provides a clear framework for analyzing how a manager interacts with their team.

questions.stem: A leader ‘inspiring trust’ is best shown by:

options.B: Consistent and ethical behavior

questions.explanation: Trust is earned over time through predictable, moral actions.

questions.stem: The primary goal of a leader is to:

options.B: Influence others toward goal achievement
options.D: Create as many rules as possible

questions.explanation: The 'reason for being' for any leader is getting the group across the finish line.

questions.stem: Leadership is a:

options.B: Continuous process

questions.explanation: Leadership doesn't stop; it requires daily maintenance and influence.

questions.stem: A leader's 'conceptual skill' is the ability to:

options.B: See the organization as a whole

questions.explanation: It is the 'big picture' thinking required at the highest levels of leadership.

questions.stem: Human skills are most important at:

options.B: Middle management only

questions.explanation: No matter how high you go, you are still working with human beings.

questions.stem: Technical skills are most important at:

options.B: Middle management

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to know how the actual 'work' is done to guide those doing it.

questions.stem: Conceptual skills are most important at:

options.B: Middle management

questions.explanation: Top leaders deal with abstract strategies rather than hands-on tasks.

questions.stem: Management is the process of:

options.B: Doing everything yourself

questions.explanation: The essence of management is using resources (including people) to achieve results.

questions.stem: The 14 principles of management were developed by:

options.B: Henri Fayol

questions.explanation: Fayol's principles form the backbone of classical management theory.

questions.stem: The 'Unity of Command' principle means:

options.B: An employee should receive orders from only one superior
options.C: The team should work in unison

questions.explanation: Receiving orders from multiple bosses causes confusion and conflict.

questions.stem: The 'Scalar Chain' refers to:

options.B: The line of authority from top management to the lowest ranks

questions.explanation: It describes the 'ladder' of hierarchy within an organization.

questions.stem: Scientific Management was pioneered by:

options.B: Frederick Taylor

questions.explanation: Taylor focused on optimizing efficiency through 'science' and time-motion studies.

questions.stem: The 'Hawthorne Studies' highlighted the importance of:

options.B: Social and psychological factors at work

questions.explanation: These studies showed that feeling cared for and noticed increases productivity more than physical changes.

questions.stem: Theory X assumes that employees are:

options.B: Inherently lazy and dislike work

questions.explanation: Theory X managers believe they must force or bribe people to work.

questions.stem: Theory Y assumes that employees are:

options.B: Creative and seek responsibility

questions.explanation: Theory Y assumes people naturally want to do a good job if given the chance.

questions.stem: Maslow’s hierarchy of needs begins with:

options.B: Safety needs

questions.explanation: The most basic needs are biological, like food, water, and sleep.

questions.stem: The highest level of Maslow’s hierarchy is:

options.B: Belonging

questions.explanation: This is the desire to become everything one is capable of becoming.

questions.stem: Herzberg’s two-factor theory includes:

options.B: Hygiene factors and motivators

questions.explanation: Hygiene factors prevent unhappiness, but only motivators create true satisfaction.

questions.stem: Hygiene factors (Herzberg) prevent:

options.B: Dissatisfaction

questions.explanation: Things like pay and policy won't make people 'happy,' but if they are bad, they make people 'unhappy'.

questions.stem: Motivators (Herzberg) lead to:

options.B: Satisfaction and high performance

questions.explanation: Factors like recognition and growth are what actually inspire people to excel.

questions.stem: Planning involves:

options.A: Checking what happened in the past
options.B: Setting goals and deciding how to achieve them

questions.explanation: Planning is the forward-looking function of management.

questions.stem: Organizing involves:

options.B: Assigning tasks and allocating resources

questions.explanation: Organizing is about putting the 'puzzle pieces' (people and tools) in the right places.

questions.stem: Controlling involves:

options.A: Monitoring performance and taking corrective action
options.B: Telling people exactly what to do every second

questions.explanation: Controlling is checking if the plan is working and fixing it if it isn't.

questions.stem: The first step in the decision-making process is:

options.B: Identifying the problem

questions.explanation: You cannot find a solution if you don't know what you are trying to solve.

questions.stem: "Synergy" means:

options.B: The whole is greater than the sum of its parts

questions.explanation: Synergy occurs when teamwork produces results that individuals couldn't achieve alone.

questions.stem: Organizational culture is:

options.A: The types of food eaten at the office
options.B: The shared values and beliefs of the organization

questions.explanation: Culture is the 'personality' of the workplace.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship between leadership and motivation?

options.B: Effective leadership creates conditions that inspire intrinsic motivation in followers
options.C: Motivation is solely a product of financial incentives
options.D: Leadership decreases motivation by increasing employee pressure

questions.explanation: Leadership is the catalyst that activates motivation.

questions.stem: The concept that 'followers promote what the leader desires' suggests that effective leadership results in:

options.B: Genuine follower commitment and internalization of organizational goals

questions.explanation: Successful leadership makes the organization's goals feel like the follower's personal goals.

questions.stem: Which level of management requires a balance of all three skills — technical, human, and conceptual?

options.B: Top management only

questions.explanation: Middle managers bridge the gap between high-level strategy and low-level technical work.

questions.stem: In Likert's System-1, subordinates are described as having:

options.B: Equal say in decision-making

questions.explanation: The exploitive style is based on total control because the manager doesn't trust the staff.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents how democratic leadership improves organizational decisions?

options.A: The leader's experience alone ensures quality
options.B: Diverse perspectives from multiple participants result in more informed and balanced decisions

questions.explanation: Multiple viewpoints catch errors that a single person might miss.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents how a manager's focus differs from a leader's focus?

options.B: Focus on innovation
options.C: Focus on the bottom line and immediate financial results

questions.explanation: Managers are typically held accountable for near-term metrics and outputs.

questions.stem: Which of the following reflects a leader's 'long-range view' in practice?

options.A: Focusing on this month's sales targets
options.B: Investing in employee development for future organizational capacity

questions.explanation: Developing people is a long-term investment that yields results years into the future.

questions.stem: The "Span of Control" refers to:

options.A: The number of subordinates a manager can effectively supervise
options.B: The power a CEO has over the board
options.C: The physical area of a factory
options.D: The length of a project's timeline

questions.explanation: It determines how many people report directly to a single manager.

questions.stem: Decentralization is the:

options.B: Distribution of decision-making authority throughout the organization
options.D: Consolidation of power at the headquarters

questions.explanation: Decentralization pushes power down to the people closest to the action.

questions.stem: A "Flat" organizational structure has:

options.B: Few levels of hierarchy and a wide span of control

questions.explanation: Flat structures have very few 'middle managers' between the top and bottom.

questions.stem: Ethics in management refers to:

options.B: Moral principles that govern a manager's behavior
options.C: Following only the legal minimum requirements
options.D: Ignoring the environmental impact of business

questions.explanation: Ethical management involves doing what is 'right' even when it isn't required by law.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the primary focus of Section B in the management course?

options.B: B. Motivation and group dynamics

questions.explanation: Section B typically transitions from individual leadership to the psychological aspects of motivation and collective group behavior.

questions.stem: Motivation is best described as:

options.B: B. The inner drive that directs and sustains behavior toward a goal
options.C: C. A formal set of rules and regulations
options.D: D. The physical strength of an employee

questions.explanation: Motivation is the psychological process that gives purpose and direction to behavior.

questions.stem: In the context of management, 'Intrinsic Motivation' comes from:

options.B: B. Threat of dismissal
options.C: C. Personal satisfaction and the enjoyment of the work itself

questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation is internal; it is the natural satisfaction derived from performing the task itself.

questions.stem: Extrinsic motivation is driven by:

options.B: B. External rewards such as pay, recognition, or avoiding punishment

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivators are external factors provided by the organization to encourage performance.

questions.stem: According to Maslow’s Hierarchy, which needs must be satisfied before social needs become dominant?

options.B: B. Esteem and recognition

questions.explanation: Maslow’s theory is progressive; basic survival and security needs must be met before social belonging becomes a priority.

questions.stem: A manager who believes employees must be coerced, controlled, or threatened with punishment to work is following:

options.B: B. Theory X

questions.explanation: Theory X assumes employees are naturally lazy and require external control to be productive.

questions.stem: Which theory suggests that satisfaction and dissatisfaction are not opposite ends of the same scale?

options.B: B. Vroom's Expectancy Theory

questions.explanation: Herzberg argued that factors leading to satisfaction (motivators) are distinct from those preventing dissatisfaction (hygiene factors).

questions.stem: In Herzberg's theory, which of the following is considered a 'Hygiene Factor'?

options.B: B. Growth

questions.explanation: Hygiene factors, such as working conditions and salary, prevent dissatisfaction but do not necessarily inspire high-level motivation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a 'Motivator' according to Herzberg?

options.B: B. Supervision

questions.explanation: Motivators are intrinsic to the job and lead to positive satisfaction and higher performance.

questions.stem: The 'ERG' in Alderfer's motivation theory stands for:

options.B: B. Existence, Relatedness, and Growth

questions.explanation: Alderfer condensed Maslow's five levels into three categories: Existence, Relatedness, and Growth.

questions.stem: McClelland’s Need Theory identifies three needs. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.B: B. Need for Affiliation

questions.explanation: McClelland focused on secondary psychological needs: Achievement (nAch), Affiliation (nAff), and Power (nPow).

questions.stem: High achievers (nAch) prefer tasks that have:

options.B: B. High risk with high rewards
options.C: C. Intermediate risk and provide immediate feedback

questions.explanation: High achievers enjoy challenges but want a realistic chance of success and immediate feedback.

questions.stem: Vroom’s Expectancy Theory formula is:

options.B: B. Motivation = Expectancy × Instrumentality × Valence

questions.explanation: This multiplicative formula suggests that if any component is zero, motivation is zero.

questions.stem: In Expectancy Theory, 'Valence' refers to:

options.A: A. The probability that effort leads to performance
options.B: B. The belief that performance leads to a reward
options.C: C. The value or importance an individual places on a particular reward
options.D: D. The physical energy of the employee

questions.explanation: Valence is the degree of attraction or desire an individual has for the outcome.

questions.stem: Equity Theory (Stacy Adams) suggests that people are motivated by:

options.B: B. Perceptions of fairness relative to others

questions.explanation: People compare their ratio of inputs and outcomes to those of others to judge fairness.

questions.stem: A 'Reference Group' in Equity Theory is:

options.B: B. Others with whom an individual compares their own input-outcome ratio
options.C: C. The customers of the firm
options.D: D. A group of technical experts

questions.explanation: Comparison is the core of equity theory; referents are the people we measure ourselves against.

questions.stem: Goal-Setting Theory suggests that goals should be:

options.B: B. Specific and challenging
options.D: D. Set only by management without employee input

questions.explanation: Specific, difficult (but attainable) goals lead to higher performance than 'do your best' goals.

questions.stem: Reinforcement Theory is based on the idea that behavior is a function of:

options.B: B. Innate drives

questions.explanation: Developed by B.F. Skinner, this theory posits that behavior followed by positive consequences is likely to be repeated.

questions.stem: What is 'Negative Reinforcement'?

options.B: B. Withdrawing an unpleasant consequence when a desired behavior occurs

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement encourages behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus when the employee does well.

questions.stem: What is 'Extinction' in reinforcement theory?

options.B: B. Providing a bonus
options.C: C. Withholding reinforcement to decrease the frequency of an undesired behavior

questions.explanation: If a behavior is not reinforced, it eventually fades away or goes 'extinct'.

questions.stem: Job Enrichment involves:

options.A: A. Giving an employee more tasks of the same level
options.B: B. Increasing the depth of a job by giving more responsibility and control
options.C: C. Moving an employee from one job to another

questions.explanation: Enrichment is vertical expansion; it adds meaning and autonomy to the role.

questions.stem: Job Enlargement involves:

options.A: A. Adding more tasks of a similar nature to a job
options.B: B. Increasing responsibility

questions.explanation: Enlargement is horizontal expansion; it increases the variety of tasks to reduce boredom.

questions.stem: A 'Group' in organizational behavior is defined as:

options.A: A. Any collection of people in a building
options.B: B. Two or more individuals who interact and are interdependent to achieve objectives
options.C: C. A list of employees on a payroll
options.D: D. Competitors in the same market

questions.explanation: Interaction and mutual goals are the defining characteristics of a formal or informal group.

questions.stem: A 'Formal Group' is one that is:

options.B: B. Defined by the organization's structure with designated work assignments

questions.explanation: Formal groups are officially created by management to perform specific organizational tasks.

questions.stem: An 'Informal Group' arises from:

options.B: B. Strategic planning sessions
options.C: C. Social contact and common interests among employees

questions.explanation: Informal groups are natural social groupings that form based on shared values or friendships.

questions.stem: The first stage of group development is:

options.B: B. Norming

questions.explanation: In the Forming stage, members get to know each other and establish ground rules.

questions.stem: The 'Storming' stage of group development is characterized by:

options.B: B. Intragroup conflict and competition for roles

questions.explanation: During Storming, members test boundaries and conflict often arises over leadership and direction.

questions.stem: The 'Norming' stage is when:

options.B: B. Close relationships develop and the group demonstrates cohesiveness
options.C: C. Conflicts are at their highest
options.D: D. The task is finally completed

questions.explanation: Norming is the stage where the group settles into a rhythm and establishes common expectations.

questions.stem: The 'Performing' stage is characterized by:

options.B: B. High task orientation and focus on achieving results

questions.explanation: In the Performing stage, the group's energy is channeled into the actual work at hand.

questions.stem: Group 'Cohesiveness' refers to:

options.A: A. The size of the group
options.B: B. The degree to which members are attracted to each other and motivated to stay in the group
options.D: D. The technical skills of the group

questions.explanation: Cohesiveness is the 'social glue' that keeps the group together.

questions.stem: What is 'Groupthink'?

options.B: B. A phenomenon where the desire for harmony results in irrational decision-making
options.C: C. A type of computer software

questions.explanation: Groupthink occurs when pressure to agree prevents critical evaluation of alternative ideas.

questions.stem: Social Loafing is:

options.A: A. Working harder in a group
options.B: B. The tendency for individuals to expend less effort when working collectively than when working individually
options.C: C. A type of social networking
options.D: D. Being the leader of a social group

questions.explanation: This happens when individual accountability is lost in a group setting.

questions.stem: A 'Team' differs from a 'Group' because in a team:

options.B: B. Performance is simply the sum of individual contributions
options.C: C. Efforts result in a level of performance that is greater than the sum of individual inputs

questions.explanation: Teams aim for collective performance and mutual accountability to produce synergy.

questions.stem: In a 'Self-Managed Team', members:

options.A: A. Have no supervisor and take on traditional management responsibilities
options.B: B. Only manage their own personal schedules

questions.explanation: Self-managed teams handle their own planning and quality control without direct oversight.

questions.stem: Communication is defined as:

options.B: B. The transfer and understanding of meaning
options.C: C. Sending an email without receiving a reply

questions.explanation: Communication requires both the transmission and the accurate understanding of the message.

questions.stem: The 'Source' or 'Sender' in the communication process:

options.B: B. Initiates the message by encoding a thought

questions.explanation: The sender is the person who has the information or idea they wish to convey.

questions.stem: Encoding involves:

options.A: A. Translating thoughts into a symbolic form
options.B: B. Reading a message

questions.explanation: Encoding is the process of putting the idea into a medium that can be transmitted.

questions.stem: The 'Channel' is:

options.A: A. The person who receives the message
options.B: B. The medium through which the message travels
options.C: C. The noise in the background

questions.explanation: Channels include face-to-face talk, emails, phone calls, or written memos.

questions.stem: Decoding is the process of:

options.B: B. Selecting a channel
options.C: C. Translating the received symbols into a meaningful thought

questions.explanation: Decoding is performed by the receiver to make sense of the incoming symbols.

questions.stem: 'Noise' in communication refers to:

options.B: B. Factors that distort the clarity of the message

questions.explanation: Noise can be physical, psychological, or semantic factors that disrupt communication.

questions.stem: The 'Feedback' loop in communication:

options.B: B. Checks the success of the communication
options.D: D. Always happens at the start

questions.explanation: Feedback confirms whether the message was received as intended.

questions.stem: Non-verbal communication includes:

options.B: B. Written memos
options.C: C. Body language, facial expressions, and tone of voice

questions.explanation: Non-verbal cues often carry more meaning than the actual words spoken.

questions.stem: Downward communication flows from:

options.B: B. Superiors to subordinates
options.C: C. Peers at the same level

questions.explanation: This includes instructions, feedback on performance, and organizational policies.

questions.stem: Upward communication provides:

options.B: B. Feedback to higher-ups about performance and ideas

questions.explanation: Upward flow allows management to understand employee sentiment and issues.

questions.stem: Lateral (Horizontal) communication occurs between:

options.B: B. Members of the same work group or same level
options.D: D. The company and the media

questions.explanation: Lateral communication is essential for coordination between departments.

questions.stem: The 'Grapevine' is the organization's:

options.B: B. Informal communication network

questions.explanation: The grapevine is the unofficial network of rumors and informal information.

questions.stem: A barrier to communication called 'Filtering' is:

options.B: B. Purposely manipulating information so it will be seen more favorably

questions.explanation: Filtering involves telling the receiver what they want to hear to avoid trouble.

questions.stem: Selective Perception means:

options.B: B. Receivers projecting their own needs into the message as they decode it

questions.explanation: We 'hear' what we want or expect to hear based on our own background.

questions.stem: Information Overload occurs when:

options.B: B. The information inflow exceeds an individual's processing capacity
options.D: D. A report is too short

questions.explanation: Too much data leads to stress and the inability to make effective decisions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a 'semantic' barrier to communication?

options.B: B. Differences in the meaning and usage of words

questions.explanation: Semantic barriers arise when people use different definitions for words or jargon.

questions.stem: Organizational Conflict is:

options.B: B. A process where one party perceives another has negatively affected something they care about
options.C: C. Physical fighting in the office

questions.explanation: Conflict is perception-based and involves goals, values, or interests.

questions.stem: The 'Traditional View' of conflict is that it is:

options.B: B. Harmful and must be avoided
options.D: D. A sign of high innovation

questions.explanation: Early management theories viewed conflict as a sign of poor management.

questions.stem: The 'Interactionist View' of conflict suggests that:

options.A: A. Conflict should be eliminated immediately
options.B: B. A minimal level of conflict is necessary to keep a group viable
options.C: C. Only task conflict is okay
options.D: D. Conflict is a waste of time

questions.explanation: This view encourages constructive conflict that prevents group stagnation.

questions.stem: 'Functional Conflict' is conflict that:

options.B: B. Supports the goals of the group and improves performance

questions.explanation: Constructive conflict leads to better ideas and solutions.

questions.stem: 'Dysfunctional Conflict' is conflict that:

options.B: B. Hinders group performance

questions.explanation: Destructive conflict wastes energy and creates hostility without benefit.

questions.stem: Task Conflict relates to:

options.B: B. The content and goals of the work
options.C: C. How the work gets done
options.D: D. Who sits where in the office

questions.explanation: Task conflict is disagreement over 'what' the group is trying to achieve.

questions.stem: Relationship Conflict relates to:

options.B: B. Interpersonal incompatibilities and friction

questions.explanation: This is almost always dysfunctional as it focuses on personal dislike.

questions.stem: Process Conflict relates to:

options.B: B. How the work gets done

questions.explanation: Process conflict is a dispute over delegation and methods used to complete a task.

questions.stem: A 'Competing' conflict-handling intention is:

options.B: B. I win, you lose (High assertiveness, low cooperation)

questions.explanation: In competing, one person seeks to satisfy their own interests regardless of others.

questions.stem: An 'Avoiding' conflict-handling intention is:

options.B: B. Withdrawing from or suppressing the conflict

questions.explanation: Avoiding is characterized by being unassertive and uncooperative.

questions.stem: A 'Collaborating' conflict-handling intention aims for:

options.B: B. A Win-Win solution that fully satisfies all parties

questions.explanation: Collaboration involves open sharing of information to find a creative solution for all.

questions.stem: An 'Accommodating' intention is when a party:

options.B: B. Places the opponent's interests above their own

questions.explanation: Accommodating is high cooperation but low assertiveness ('I lose, you win').

questions.stem: 'Compromising' involves:

options.B: B. Each party giving up something

questions.explanation: Compromising is a mid-point where neither party gets everything, but both get something.

questions.stem: Negotiation is:

options.B: B. A process in which parties exchange goods/services and attempt to agree on a rate

questions.explanation: Negotiation is the primary tool for resolving conflict over resource allocation.

questions.stem: 'Distributive Bargaining' is characterized as:

options.B: B. Win-Lose (A fixed pie of resources)

questions.explanation: In distributive bargaining, any gain I make is a loss for you.

questions.stem: 'Integrative Bargaining' aims for:

options.B: B. Win-Win (Expanding the pie)

questions.explanation: Integrative bargaining seeks long-term relationship building and mutual benefit.

questions.stem: BATNA stands for:

options.A: A. Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement
options.B: B. Better Always Than Never Agreeing
options.C: C. Basic Agreement Toward New Alliances
options.D: D. Buying All Technical New Assets

questions.explanation: Your BATNA is your walk-away point; the lowest value you will accept.

questions.stem: Power (in Section B) is defined as:

options.B: B. The capacity that A has to influence the behavior of B so B acts in accordance with A’s wishes

questions.explanation: Power is about dependency; the more B depends on A, the more power A has over B.

questions.stem: The most important aspect of power is that it is a function of:

options.B: B. Dependency

questions.explanation: If you control something that others need, they are dependent on you, giving you power.

questions.stem: Expert Power is base on:

options.B: B. Influence wielded as a result of expertise, special skill, or knowledge

questions.explanation: Specialists often have power because others need their unique skills.

questions.stem: Referent Power is based on:

options.B: B. Identification with a person who has desirable traits

questions.explanation: It is essentially charisma power; people follow you because they admire you.

questions.stem: The 'Legitimate Power' comes from:

options.B: B. The formal structural position in an organization

questions.explanation: It is the power people accept because of a person's rank in the hierarchy.

questions.stem: Influence Tactics include 'Rational Persuasion', which is:

options.B: B. Using logical arguments and factual evidence
options.D: D. Asking for a favor based on friendship

questions.explanation: Rational persuasion is generally the most effective tactic across organizational levels.

questions.stem: The influence tactic 'Ingratiation' involves:

options.B: B. Using flattery, praise, or friendly behavior

questions.explanation: Ingratiation is being extra nice to someone before making a request.

questions.stem: The influence tactic 'Pressure' involves:

options.B: B. Using warnings, repeated demands, and threats

questions.explanation: Pressure is often the least effective tactic and can cause resentment.

questions.stem: Organizational Politics refers to:

options.B: B. Activities that influence the distribution of advantages in the organization

questions.explanation: Politics is 'power in action'; it involves building coalitions and self-promotion.

questions.stem: Political behavior is more likely when:

options.B: B. Resources are scarce and roles are ambiguous
options.C: C. Everything is clear and documented
options.D: D. There is only one employee

questions.explanation: Uncertainty and limited budgets cause people to fight for resources.

questions.stem: Impression Management (IM) is the process by which:

options.B: B. Individuals attempt to control the impression others form of them

questions.explanation: IM techniques include self-promotion and excuses to maintain a positive image.

questions.stem: Organizational Culture is often described as:

options.B: B. The shared values and beliefs that shape how members think and act
options.D: D. The layout of the cafeteria

questions.explanation: Culture is the 'social glue' and the personality of the organization.

questions.stem: A 'Dominant Culture' is:

options.A: A. A culture only for managers
options.B: B. The core values shared by a majority of the organization’s members
options.C: C. A culture based on force
options.D: D. The culture of the competitors

questions.explanation: The dominant culture gives an organization its distinct personality.

questions.stem: 'Subcultures' are:

options.A: A. Cultures that oppose the main one
options.B: B. Minicultures within an organization, defined by department or geography

questions.explanation: Subcultures form around shared work experiences or specific professional backgrounds.

questions.stem: A 'Strong Culture' is characterized by:

options.A: A. High physical strength of employees
options.B: B. Core values that are intensely held and widely shared
options.C: C. Lots of rules in a book

questions.explanation: In strong cultures, behavior is guided by shared values rather than strict supervision.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of organizational culture?

options.B: B. Conveys a sense of identity
options.D: D. Facilitates commitment to the collective

questions.explanation: Culture's role is to facilitate commitment to something larger than the self.

questions.stem: Culture is transmitted to employees through:

options.B: B. Genetic inheritance

questions.explanation: Rituals and symbols reinforce the culture's values to the workforce.

questions.stem: Socialization is the process that:

options.B: B. Adapts employees to the organization's culture

questions.explanation: Socialization helps new hires learn 'how we do things around here'.

questions.stem: A 'Spiritual Organization' culture is one that:

options.B: B. Recognizes that people have an inner life nourished by meaningful work

questions.explanation: Workplace spirituality focuses on purpose, ethics, and community.

questions.stem: Resistance to change is:

options.B: B. A natural human tendency based on fear of the unknown and habit
options.C: C. Only found in lazy employees

questions.explanation: Change threatens the 'comfort zone' and established ways of working.

questions.stem: An individual source of resistance to change is 'Habit', which means:

options.B: B. Relying on programmed responses to handle life’s complexities

questions.explanation: To cope with many daily decisions, we rely on habits. Change disrupts these.

questions.stem: An organizational source of resistance to change is 'Structural Inertia', which means:

options.B: B. Built-in mechanisms to produce stability that act against change

questions.explanation: Organizations are built for stability, making them naturally resist change.

questions.stem: Lewin's Three-Step Model for change consists of:

options.B: B. Unfreezing, Movement, Refreezing

questions.explanation: You must break old patterns (Unfreeze), implement change (Movement), and make it permanent (Refreeze).

questions.stem: In Lewin’s model, 'Unfreezing' involves:

options.B: B. Overcoming the pressures of individual resistance

questions.explanation: Unfreezing prepares the organization by showing that the current state is not sustainable.

questions.stem: In Lewin’s model, 'Refreezing' means:

options.B: B. Stabilizing a change intervention by balancing driving and restraining forces
options.C: C. Going back to old ways

questions.explanation: Without refreezing, employees will naturally drift back to old habits.

questions.stem: A 'Learning Organization' is one that has:

options.B: B. Developed the continuous capacity to adapt and change
